transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?

Hi. Well, what brought me in is... I just can't stop jumping out of my skin lately. I do a lot of repair work, and if a breaker snaps, or a tool drops on the concrete, or even if somebody just comes up behind me... I completely jump. And my heart just keeps hammering in my chest, long after everyone else has already moved on. It's really starting to mess with me.
Did these reactions start happening after a specific frightening or traumatic event?
Yeah. It started after an arc-flash accident on a retrofit job I was doing. This has all been going on since then, so... about a year and a month now.
Do you ever find yourself reliving the arc-flash accident, such as through sudden flashbacks, unwanted memories, or nightmares?

Yeah, I do. It happens... well, just out of nowhere, really. I could be doing something completely normal, like just loading my tools into the back of the truck, and suddenly I'll just see that bright flash right in my head. Or I'll hear the trainee yelling. It just knocks me sideways, man. It feels exactly like it's happening all over again.
Do you find yourself going out of your way to avoid places, activities, or people that remind you of the accident?

Yeah, I do. I... I make excuses not to go near certain panels or breakers now. Even whole job sites, if they remind me too much of it. I try to avoid talking about that day, too, because once it starts playing in my head, I just can't shut it off.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient experienced a traumatic arc-flash electrical accident 13 months ago and exhibits classic features of post-traumatic stress disorder, including intrusive re-experiencing (flashbacks), active avoidance of trauma-related triggers and discussions, and persistent autonomic hyperarousal with an exaggerated startle response.

confirmed_symptoms: Flashbacks and vivid re-experiencing of the visual and auditory trauma memories (seeing the flash, hearing trainee yelling)
Avoidance of electrical panels, breakers, and job sites that remind of the incident
Avoidance of conversations about the trauma
Exaggerated startle response to sudden noises or people approaching
Prolonged physiological reactivity/tachycardia following startle triggers

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Symptoms have persisted for approximately 1 year and 1 month (13 months) following the incident
additional_requirements: Exposure to a life-threatening or catastrophic workplace accident (arc-flash explosion)
